title: Curavia
tagline: A hospital operating system, from front desk to pharmacy.
summary: Multi-hospital software where one hospital can never see another’s patients. A query that forgets its hospital crashes instead of leaking data.
problem: Hospital data is the worst thing to leak. Forgetting one filter in one query shouldn’t be enough to do it.
note: In development. Orders, safety checks and referrals are being built now.
features: Four layers of tenant isolation, including PostgreSQL row-level security
A permissions matrix that generates its own tests
A hash-chained audit log that can’t be quietly edited
TenantScopeMissing: unscoped queries crash on purpose
why: Hospital records are the worst thing to leak. Curavia is a hospital operating system for Nigerian hospitals, from front desk and triage to lab, pharmacy, billing and wards, built so one forgotten filter can never expose another hospital’s patients.
hard: Including PostgreSQL row-level security; a query with no hospital scope crashes with TenantScopeMissing.
A role-by-action matrix generates the permission tests.
An audit log you can trust
Hash-chained, so a quiet edit breaks the chain.
